messages:
acme-client: Hey, running into a weird issue with streaming SSE. Started a long chat stream (~6k tokens) and we get a 429 in the middle of the stream. Client receives partial output then connection drops. No `retry-after` header, and invoices show tokens counted twice for the same prompt. Happening intermittently since yesterday, ~10% of sessions. Request id: rid_0a9f3c. Can share logs.

marie-support: Sorry you hit this — that sounds bad. A few quick Qs: which SDK/version or raw SSE curl are you using? Is the auth token rotating mid-session? Any proxy/load balancer between client and our SSE endpoint? Also can you paste the raw SSE log around the 429?

acme-client: Using our node client that wraps EventSource (eventsource npm). Not rotating token. No corporate proxy, direct from user's browser. Repro steps: 1) open SSE to /v1/streams/chat with Authorization: Bearer <key> 2) stream until ~2500 tokens generated 3) server emits `event: error` with data: {"code":429,"message":"rate limit"} then connection closes. Sample response chunk log: ```
event: message
data: {"id":"c_1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...long text chunk"}}],"meta":{"consumed_tokens":2489}}

event: error
data: {"code":429,"message":"quota exceeded"}
```

marie-support: Good repro, thanks. Two likely overlapping issues: (A) rate limiter counting tokens in near-real time and tripping mid-stream if token budget is hit; (B) client reconnect semantics causing duplicate/recounted tokens on resume. We're going to check headers we send on the 429 response (x-rate-limit, x-consumed-tokens, retry-after).@kai-platform can you sanity-check our SSE 429 header shape?

kai-platform: quick note — the SSE path should include `x-consumed-tokens` and `x-rate-limit-reset` on 429s, but older infra sometimes omitted `retry-after`. I'll check the rid. If `retry-after` missing that's a bug in the rate limiter middleware.

dan-metrics: pulling metrics for rid_0a9f3c... I see a short burst from the connection: token ingestion rate spikes at close to 350 tokens/sec. Quota window for that key is 150k tokens/min with a short-burst cap that we apply per-connection. The burst cap looks like it triggered a mid-stream enforcement for that connection at 2026-12-04T18:02:17Z. The billing pipeline shows two consumed-token records for the same prompt id when the client reconnects within 3s.

marie-support: ok that explains the 429 origin. Client reconnects quickly and replays from last event id — server treats replayed chunks as new consumption until finalization handshake completes. We have known edge-case: if a client reconnects without honoring backoff, the runtime can double-count partial token windows. Workarounds: 1) client should implement exponential backoff on 429 and avoid immediate reconnect; 2) use a short, server-issued session id to resume instead of replaying from the beginning (we'll explain).

acme-client: For (2) — how do we request a session id? We didn't see that in the docs. Right now we just reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` header and event ids from the stream.

marie-support: Today our SSE supports `Last-Event-ID` for idempotency but the resume path is best-effort only for idempotent streams. We recently shipped a session resume token in the response for big streams on Dedicated customers, but hosted paths may not always return it. Short-term: add a client-side dedupe filter by tracking server `choice.id` or `chunk checksums` to ignore duplicates on reconnect. Also set a 429 backoff: start at 1s, double up to 16s and abort after 5 attempts.

kai-platform: Adding to that — we can push a small infra change to always include `retry-after` on SSE 429s and emit `x-final-token-count` on the session close event. I'll spike that and loop eng-oncall if it looks risky.

acme-client: Appreciate it. Is there a safe repro we can run to demonstrate double-charge so we can attach to our billing ticket? I can run a script against a non-prod key.

marie-support: Yes, please run with these steps (sanitized): ```bash
# create long generation that forces bursts
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -N 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -d '{"model":"open-lite-3","prompt":"<~6k token prompt>","stream":true}' 
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/streams/chat | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Observe the moment of the `event: error`. Then immediately reconnect (simulate client) and note invoices in `/v1/usage` for the key for that minute window. If you see two consumption batches for same prompt id within <10s, we reproduce billing double-count.

acme-client: Will run now — sharing results in ~15m. One more: on our side we do small per-chunk ack to our UI; if we get duplicate chunks we de-dupe by `choice.id` but sometimes the chunks are cut mid-token and checksum changes. Might need server to provide boundaries.

dan-metrics: That checksum issue is real — partial chunk boundaries differ on resume. Adding a stable `chunk_index` or `chunk_boundary_hash` would help clients dedupe. Flagging in metrics backlog.

deploy-bot: deploy: infra-ratefix (pr 4821) promoted to staging at 2026-12-05T01:10:32Z — includes always-send `retry-after` on SSE 429 and `x-consumed-tokens` header.

kai-platform: Good — once that lands we'll have better client guidance. Longer-term eng-oncall, can we add a `session_resume_token` in the SSE hello event? That lets clients ask server to resume without re-consuming already-accounted tokens.

eng-oncall: Acknowledged. I created ENG-1267 to implement `session_resume_token` and `x-final-token-count` on session close. Also will add server side dedupe to the billing pipeline for retries within 30s for same session id. For now, marie-support please advise Acme to apply backoff + client-side dedupe by `choice.id` and avoid immediate reconnects.

marie-support: acme-client — thanks for the patience. If you can run the repro and paste the `curl -v` output + the `/v1/usage` snapshot I'll attach to the billing ticket and we can do a provisional credit if we confirm double-charge.

acme-client: Posting logs: ```
> GET /v1/streams/chat HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.example
> Authorization: Bearer sk_test_xxx
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
...
event: message
data: {"id":"c_1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}],"meta":{"consumed_tokens":2494}}
event: error
data: {"code":429,"message":"quota exceeded"}
< x-consumed-tokens: 2494
< x-rate-limit-reset: 1701823337

# immediate reconnect (client)
> GET /v1/streams/chat HTTP/1.1
> Last-Event-ID: c_1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
event: message
data: {"id":"c_2","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}],"meta":{"consumed_tokens":7}}
```

marie-support: Thanks — that shows the issue: we returned `x-consumed-tokens` on the 429 in this log which is good, but your immediate reconnect replayed and consumed new tokens. We'll file the billing attach and proceed with ENG-1267.

acme-client: Ok sounds good. One last question: is there a recommended check for client-side to avoid mid-stream 429? Like check `x-rate-limit-remaining` on every chunk?

kai-platform: You can read `x-consumed-tokens` and `x-rate-limit-remaining` on streaming chunks when provided, but not every chunk includes headers (SSE chunks are events). Best pattern: track `meta.consumed_tokens` in the event payload, and if you see it's within 1-2% of your quota, pause generation or request a new session key. Also apply conservative reconnect backoff.

marie-support: Closing loop: we'll keep this thread updated — escalated to ENG and billing. If you need an interim credit, open the billing ticket and reference rid_0a9f3c and ENG-1267. Thanks everyone :pray:
